statements.quote: Students who withdrew from the study were not included in the data analysis, and their questionnaires were not collected. Therefore, none were excluded from the collected questionnaires.

statements.quote: As shown in Table 1, the designed prompts aim to guide students using ChatGPT to solve MCT step by step, stimulating their mathematical creativity.
statements.locator: PDF p. 6 (printed p. 44), Procedure, paragraph after Figure 2; prompt materials are printed in Table 1 on PDF p. 7 (printed p. 45).

statements.quote: All human-ChatGPT interactions were automatically recorded via the platform. The interaction logs included students’ input prompts, ChatGPT’s responses and the interaction time, and were sequentially numbered for subsequent analysis and verification.
statements.locator: PDF p. 6 (printed p. 44), Procedure, paragraph after Figure 2: existence and contents of interaction logs, with no access offer.

statements.quote: As shown in Table 3, the baseline task adapted from Kattou et al. (2013) was used to measure all students’ initial mathematical creativity.
statements.locator: PDF p. 8 (printed p. 46), Measures, Mathematical creativity baseline; the baseline material is printed in Table 3.

statements.quote: The MCT was adapted from Lee and Seo (2003) to measure mathematical creativity. The initial MCT included five mathematical open-ended tasks. Notably, one task (regular hexagon problem) was excluded from the adapted version due to its low difficulty index (García-García et al., 2024). Salazar Tornel et al. (2022) also argued that it could not differentiate students’ levels of mathematical creativity, as it lacked complexity. To better assess mathematical creativity, four more challenging tasks were chosen. The adapted version underwent internal consistency testing, yielding results that demonstrated very high reliability. It includes the following tasks (as shown in Figure 3):

statements.quote: In Task 1, all correct solutions were classified based on Lee and Seo’s (2003) scoring table (see Table 4).

notes: Checked 2026-10-09. Read all 69,559 characters of the markdown in six contiguous chunks, including the complete references, author contributions, funding and final copyright/citation text. The source is the 21-page published article, printed pp. 39-59; there is no appendix or identified supplement. Verified the quoted passages directly against PyMuPDF text from the stated pages; quotation wording and punctuation are preserved, with PDF line wrapping normalized to spaces. No explicit research-data/code availability statement, on-request offer, preregistration statement or repository URL was found. The statements retained below concern data retention and recording, pointers to materials printed within the article, data-curation credits and the article's license; none promises public access to participant records. The screening form's data_url and code_url are both empty. PDF URI annotations contained literature references, the article DOI and its copyright-license link, rather than a study-data repository. The license URL https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/ returned HTTP 200; that license applies to the article, not an identified data deposit. The current publisher PDF is byte-identical to the local source. The PDF lists Zhiwei Liu, Gang Li, Haode Zuo, Yongjing Lu and Jue Feng, while the landing-page metadata omits Gang Li; title and DOI match, and the verified first author Zhiwei Liu was used for the author searches. Repeated requests for the same query are consolidated in the search log, with the initial Zenodo HTTP 400 attempts retained separately. All successful searches used public APIs via Python urllib with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1, without authentication or access requests. No GitHub API requests were needed because the paper names no repository. Search hits that could not be linked to c471 are not counted as its deposits. The unrelated Zenodo Analysis_code record exposed one 41,021-byte Analysis_Code.zip under CC BY 4.0; reading it in memory identified the study as Model-disagreement-based quality control for automatic MRI segmentation and volumetric assessment of uterine leiomyomas: an internal validation study. No c471 data table was available for checking rows, columns, arm labels, outcome scores or participant texts. Consequently, no item in final.open_items can be resolved from confirmed public deposits: allocation and withdrawal counts, the complete originality scoring rule, randomization/concealment details, scorer qualifications/blinding, and possible participant overlap with c089 remain open. Printed tasks and aggregate tables in the main article are not counted as a separate deposit. Confidence is medium because the negative repository search cannot establish the absence of an unlinked or differently titled deposit, and the specified OSF endpoint filters project titles rather than author identities. No external data files were saved; the only file written is forms/data/c471.json.
